A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LLaVA-CoT work and contain the complete main text and Appendices A–F. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that the tables, figures, and supplementary material are available for comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations, training ablations, and inference-scaling experiments in Tables 2–7, plus qualitative model comparisons.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and supplies previously withheld ablation scores and averages in Table 2.

M1.justification: The four-stage tagged reasoning procedure, supervised fine-tuning, and stage-level beam search are unchanged. Sections 3 and Appendices B–D describe the same method.

E1.justification: The training-data mixture, six evaluation benchmarks, and reasoning-focused subsets are retained. The newly populated AI2D cells concern an already included benchmark, with no documented expansion of task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same base model and training variants. The inference-scaling comparators in Table 5 and VLM comparators in Table 7 are also unchanged; no comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: v3's Table 2 caption identifies mistaken use of AI2D_TEST_NO_MASK instead of AI2D_TEST. v4 supplies scores but retains the same statement that corrections are forthcoming, so whether the testing configuration was corrected remains unclear. Other stated settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 2 adds AI2D scores and complete averages to the existing original-Q&A-training and tag-removal ablations, providing limited additional evidence for those comparisons. The MMStar skill analysis, beam-size analysis, and appendix case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 8 retains seed 42, and neither version adds repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new Table 2 averages aggregate benchmark scores rather than estimate statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces withheld entries with AI2D 81.2 and average 59.0 for Direct Training, and AI2D 79.1 and average 60.9 for the variant without Structured Tags. These are newly reported values, not demonstrated performance gains over v3. Other results are unchanged.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised. The procedural descriptions and Appendix E's benchmark aggregation rules remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about autonomous structured reasoning, inference-time scaling, and performance relative to larger and closed-source models.

C2.justification: Section 4.3's interpretations of the ablations are unchanged despite the added scores. The mechanism explanations, qualitative interpretations, and computational-resource limitation in Section 5.3 are also retained.

D1.justification: The generation and verification prompts, training hyperparameters, hardware description, beam-search implementation details, and code/data/weight access information are unchanged, including Appendices B–D.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and bibliography are unchanged. No cited work or substantive positioning relative to previous research is added or removed.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v3 dated 9 January 2025 to v4 dated 16 February 2025. The substantive prose, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Replacing Table 2's dagger-marked placeholders accompanies small spacing changes and text reflow across pages 6–8. Table structures and all figures, including appendix figures, are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 makes Table 2 more complete, but its retained caption still says the wrong AI2D test variant produced incorrect results and corrections are forthcoming. The PDFs therefore do not establish whether the new scores and derived averages resolve v3's evaluation problem. With the remaining scientific content unchanged, this ambiguity prevents a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
